Reasoning: Since the voltmeter is connected across the two ends of the two series elements, and the polarity directions of u1 and u2 are consistent, the instantaneous voltage measured by the voltmeter is u = u1 + u2. Substitute the given quantities: u = 3√2[sin(ωt + 45°) + sin(ωt - 45°)] V. Using the identity sin A + sin B = 2 sin((A+B)/2) cos((A-B)/2), get u = 3√2 · 2 sin(ωt) cos45° = 3√2 · 2 · (√2/2) sin(ωt) = 6 sin(ωt) V. The peak value of this total voltage is 6 V, and the voltmeter reading is the RMS value, therefore U = 6/√2 = 3√2 V.
